transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-10-29 15:00 PT
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Recording: yes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Liam (CSM), Evan (CTO, Sablecliff), Priya (Lead ML Eng), Dana (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick readout on benchmark results vs incumbent, identify tuning wins and remaining gaps, agree next steps for load test and security docs.

00:00 Maya: alright everyone thanks for joining, we'll run about 45 minutes, quick readout then Connor will go through the numbers. can folks see the shared sheet?
00:12 Evan: yep seeing it, looks like two tabs one is our baseline and one is the redwood runs
00:20 Connor: cool, i'll start with the latency summary — we ran three prompt cohorts: short instruction (~20-40 tokens), medium chat (~120-220 tokens), and long context (~600 tokens). p50/p95 numbers are on tab 'latency-compare'.
00:40 Connor: short prompts — Redwood p50 48ms, p95 112ms; incumbent p50 62ms, p95 210ms. so about 15ms p50 and ~100ms p95 improvement there.
01:02 Priya: those are single-token generation numbers or full response? i'm asking because our app concatenates multiple turns
01:10 Connor: full response median across tokens for the prompt length bucket, so it factors in multi-token outputs — might be why the delta grows on p95
01:24 Dana: curious about warm vs cold cache — did you see big differences?
01:30 Connor: yes, cold starts add ~60-90ms for our setup; we included both warm and cold in the distribution but also provided warm-only slice. warm-only p95 for medium chat is 180ms vs incumbent 280ms.
01:46 Evan: throughput numbers? at 100 concurrent sessions how does it behave, our traffic is bursty during office hours
01:55 Connor: throughput at 100 concurrent sessions — steady-state RPS on Redwood was 380 rps for the medium chat workload; incumbent sat around 320 rps under same config. burst ramp-up showed slight queueing at 140 concurrent where latency tails spiked.
02:17 Priya: interesting. what batch sizes were you using in the tests?
02:23 Connor: automatic batching with target batch of 8 for medium — we also tried fixed batch 4 and 16; 8 was best cost/latency tradeoff. in the sheet 'batching'.
02:36 Maya: a couple of qualitative notes — quantizing to int8 saved about 28% token-cost but we did observe a slight decrease in rare-entity recall on the long-context cohort. Priya, this is the earlier quality drop you flagged?
02:50 Priya: yeah we saw a handful of edge cases where entity hallucination increased, mainly in domain-specific chemical names. that's risky for us.
03:03 Connor: understood — we have a hybrid profile idea: keep float16 for long-context prompts and int8 for short/medium where generation quality is less sensitive. cost delta still net positive.
03:18 Dana: also would like to confirm logging — we need per-request audit logs with unique request IDs to map to our SIEM. what's Redwood's export shape?
03:29 Maya: we'll send the audit log schema; we support streaming exports to S3 or pushing to your syslog endpoint. KMS support (customer-managed keys) is available for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and HSM-backed KMS integrations.
03:45 Evan: great. does the latency delta hold up with the fallback policy? if you route to a smaller model to save cost during spikes, what happens to p95?
03:56 Connor: fallback to the lighter variant increases p95 in the long tail by about 40-60ms but keeps throughput up. routing rules we tuned: prefer regional low-latency, then capacity-tier fallback. we can show the routing trace in the next deep-dive.
04:15 Priya: one anomaly — tokenization overhead on some customer prompts spiked ~30-40ms due to long unicode sequences; is that something in Redwood tokenizer or our pre-processing?
04:28 Connor: looks like test harness passed raw text; we saw same tokenization cost in the incumbents but it was amplified in the long-context runs due to KV cache warming patterns. we can add a pre-tokenize step in the pipeline for the loadtest to isolate it.
04:46 Maya: turning to cost — unit token cost after quant + batching was ~0.012 USD per 1k tokens vs incumbent ~0.017. that's in the cost tab.
05:01 Evan: nice. so practically we get better latency and lower unit cost, but quality regression on niche entity cases needs mitigation — correct summary?
05:10 Priya: yes, and we need to validate at scale, not just microbenchmarks.
05:18 Connor: agreed — recommend head-to-head 10k request load test using your production prompt set — this should surface both latency tails and quality regressions under load.
05:28 Dana: can we get the exact config used for the runs? the thread mentioned routing_v1, quant_profile_b.
05:34 Connor: i'll put the exact JSON configs in the shared drive — routing_v2 (we iterated during the run) and quant_profile_b_hybrid which is hybrid int8/float16.
05:45 Maya: security ask — Priya Dana, what's the retention length you need for audit logs?
05:52 Dana: for compliance we need 13 months, but short-term 90 day hot window is fine for the SIEM ingest.
06:02 Maya: ok we'll note that. Redwood's hosted retention defaults to 90 days for hot logs with long-term archival options. for Private you can control retention in your own store.
06:15 Evan: on the operational side, how do you handle model rollouts? we don't want surprises if field changes behavior mid-poc
06:22 Connor: rollouts can be pinned to a model version; we support canary and A/B traffic splits plus automatic rollback triggers if eval metrics regress past thresholds. we also keep per-request model metadata in traces so you can tie outputs to model versions.
06:36 Priya: one more: can we see the raw token-level traces for the top 50 slow requests? that will help us debug the long-tail
06:44 Liam: yep Connor will collect the traces and we can upload them to the shared drive with obfuscation for PHI.
06:52 Dana: PHI handling is critical — we need to ensure logs are redacted before transfer if not using our VPC
07:00 Maya: noted, we'll follow the redaction checklist unless you opt for Private.
07:07 Evan: timeline wise — if we get the config and log shape this week we'll run the 10k test early next week and reconvene after you send the security docs.
07:14 Maya: perfect. Connor anything to add on numbers?
07:19 Connor: only that one of the biggest wins was p95 reduction on medium chat where we applied KV-cache prewarming; that alone trimmed user-visible latency by ~70ms on the tail. we documented the prewarm script in 'ops' tab.
07:34 Priya: please include the script and the exact cron we used for the prewarm in the shared folder.
07:40 Connor: will do.
07:43 Maya: ok let's run through quick recap and owners — Connor to share configs and traces, Maya to send security docs, Priya to run load test, Dana to confirm retention and privacy constraints. follow-up deep-dive scheduled week of 11/9.
07:58 Evan: good meeting, thanks everyone.
08:02 Maya: thanks all, we'll send notes and repo links after this call. bye.
